observed_title: A generalization of Cramér large deviations for martingales
version: Observed arXiv:1503.06627v1, 23 March 2015; article header cites C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris I 352 (2014) 853–858; footer dated 11 juillet 2018. Editions not conflated.

read_ranges.scope: All seven PDF pages, main results, entire printed proof sketch, appendices for Lemmas 3.2/3.3 and references.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 2.1: conditional Cramér branch
assumptions: For each n, martingale differences (ξ_i,F_i), i=0,…,n, ξ_0=0, F_0={∅,Ω}; X_n=Σξ_i and 〈X〉_n=ΣE(ξ_i²|F_{i−1}).
(A1) There are fixed positive c_0,c_1, uniform in n and i, with sup_i E(exp(c_0√n|ξ_i|)|F_{i−1})≤c_1 a.s.

The source states existence of positive absolute α_0; 0≤x≤α_0√n and δ≤α_0. Source generic constants declared absolute/depending only α, but proof uses c_0,c_1; their uniformity across arbitrary models is not independently justified.
theorem_cards.statement: Both P(X_n>x)/(1−Φ(x)) and P(X_n<−x)/Φ(−x) have the form exp{θ c_{α_0}[x³/√n+x²δ²+(1+x)(log(n)/√n+δ)]}, |θ|≤1. This is a logarithmic relative error bound, not an explicit cumulant correction. The source consequence Eq(8) uses ≥x, unlike strict Eq(6); atom handling must be supplied before equating the event contracts.
proof_steps: Exponential conjugate martingale product is defined for |λ|≤c_0√n; under P_λ, X_n=B_n(λ)+Y_n(λ).
Lemma 3.1 derives absolute moments directly from u^k/k!≤e^u. Lemmas 3.2/3.3 control B_n and Ψ_n on 0≤λ≤c_0√n/4.
Lemma 3.4 tilted Kolmogorov estimate and the main theorem proof are only referred to as similar to [3]. All printed text was read; the omitted adaptation is not an independent proof certificate.
gaps: Conditional Cramér (A1) alone does not imply the relative-to-variance Bernstein condition. A uniform positive lower bound on nE(ξ_i²|F_{i−1}) is a sufficient additional assumption cited by the source.
Main theorem and Lemma 3.4 rely on an unprinted adaptation of Fan–Grama–Liu 2013 [3]; precise c_0,c_1 dependence and atom convention remain review items.

theorem_cards.label: MDP consequence: actual normalization in displayed formula
assumptions: (A1),(A2) above with fixed c_0,c_1; δ→0; a_n→∞ and a_n/√n→0.
B is a Borel subset of ℝ; B° interior and cl(B) closure.
theorem_cards.statement: The displayed MDP uses (1/a_n²)log P(X_n/a_n∈B), rate I(x)=x²/2. The paragraph calls the speed a_n, but the displayed normalization has speed a_n². This consequence does not give a normal tail ratio or saddlepoint prefactor.
proof_steps: Combine relative logarithmic tail estimate with normal tail logarithms, then tail-based one-dimensional LDP reasoning as cited to [3].
gaps: The source only cites details in [3]; no independent general-B proof is printed here. Use the displayed a_n² normalization rather than the prose speed.

theorem_cards.label: Lemmas 3.1–3.3 and printed appendix
theorem_cards.statement: E(|ξ_i|^k|F_{i−1})≤k! c_1(c_0√n)^(−k); |B_n(λ)−λ|≤c(λδ²+λ²/√n); |Ψ_n(λ)−λ²/2|≤c(λ²δ²+λ³/√n). The first absolute moment inequality also extends directly to k=2.
proof_steps: Jensen gives conditional mgf≥1; E(ξ_i e^{λξ_i}|F_{i−1})=E[ξ_i(e^{λξ_i}−1)|F_{i−1}]≥0 for λ≥0. Taylor remainder sums give the two drift bounds.

Log expansion uses u_i=E(e^{λξ_i}|F_{i−1})−1≥0. To certify the two-sided Ψ remainder, bound the absolute third-and-higher Taylor remainder plus the nonnegative quadratic log remainder. The printed intermediate inequalities omit absolute values; this local repair does not prove Lemma 3.4.
gaps: Constants in these local estimates depend on the fixed conditional exponential moment parameters; no numerical constants were derived.

transfer_boundary: Keep as a separate conditional Cramér martingale branch with fixed parameters and declared filtration; do not replace (A1) by Bernstein-relative-to-variance or present its abbreviated proof as fully independently checked. Private cube/uniform-center-radius assumptions absent.
proof_verification: Whole source read; Lemma 3.1 and local appendix algebra checked. Main theorem/Lemma 3.4 unprinted adaptations and constants dependence remain gaps.
